item.title: Mainland criticizes Taiwan authorities over 'defense' spending increase
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Mainland criticizes Taiwan authorities over 'defense' spending increase Source: chinadaily.com.cnUpdated: 2026-09-30
A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday criticized the Lai Ching-te authorities in Taiwan for increasing "defense" spending, saying the move would harm the interests of Taiwan residents and push the island into a more dangerous situation. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular news conference that the Lai authorities have adhered to a separatist "Taiwan independence" position and sought to pursue "independence" through military means and reliance on external forces. She criticized the authorities for increasingly squandering the hard-earned money of Taiwan residents. At an event in Kaohsiung on Sept 23, Lai said the authorities would allocate more than NT$1.3 trillion ($40.8 billion) in "defense" spending next year for military procurement, international cooperation and indigenous "defense" development. He said the focus would be on strengthening industries such as drones and robotics to further enhance the island's "defense capabilities". In response, Zhang said the large-scale investment in "defense" would not only reduce resources available for livelihoods and social welfare on the island and harm the immediate interests of Taiwan residents, but also push Taiwan toward a more dangerous situation. She accused the Lai authorities of dragging Taiwan residents into becoming "cannon fodder" for "Taiwan independence". "Such actions that harm and undermine Taiwan and lead to self-destruction will face strong opposition," she said. "No matter how much budget Lai allocates or how many weapons he purchases, he cannot escape the inevitable failure of 'Taiwan independence'." Related Stories

item.title: Chinese mainland welcomes public suggestions on "two systems" solution to Taiwan question: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese mainland welcomes public suggestions on "two systems" solution to Taiwan question: spokesperson Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday welcomed people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait to offer opinions and suggestions on the solution to the Taiwan question under the "one country, two systems" framework. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a media conference in response to a question about recent discussions on the "two systems" solution to the Taiwan question. Zhang said that peaceful reunification and "one country, two systems" remain the basic policy for resolving the Taiwan question and the best way to achieve national reunification, serving the interests of compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and the Chinese nation as a whole. "The reunification of the motherland is an unstoppable historical trend," she noted. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Zhang said that an increasing number of people in Taiwan have begun discussing the specific content of the solution. They are also envisioning prospects for a better future following reunification and considering the major opportunities reunification would bring to Taiwan's social and economic development, as well as the tangible benefits it would bring to the people of Taiwan, she added. "We welcome compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait to pool their wisdom and contribute more opinions and suggestions on the solution," Zhang said. She called on people on both sides to work together to create the historic achievement of national reunification and share in the great glory of national rejuvenation. Related Stories

item.title: Firm opposition to "Taiwan independence" serves common interests of China, U.S.: mainland spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Firm opposition to "Taiwan independence" serves common interests of China, U.S.: mainland spokesperson Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Firmly opposing separatist activities seeking "Taiwan independence" and maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait serve the common interests of both China and the United States, a Chinese mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference in response to a question about recent discussion over the role of the Taiwan question in China-U.S. relations. Reiterating that the Taiwan question is at the very core of China's core interests and the bedrock of the political foundation of China-U.S. relations, Zhang said that proper handling of the Taiwan question would help maintain overall stability in China-U.S. relations, while mishandling it could lead to confrontation or even conflict and push bilateral ties into a highly dangerous situation. Zhang said Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te have persisted in their separatist position and refused to recognize the 1992 Consensus, which embodies the one-China principle, while repeatedly making moves in pursuit of "Taiwan independence." "It is the main source of disruption to peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait," Zhang said, calling on people on both sides of the Strait to work together to advance national reunification. The Taiwan question stems from a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the CPC founded the People's Republic of China (PRC). The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, though the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. In a separate response to a question about remarks by a Taiwan politician, who accused the mainland of deliberately misinterpreting UN General Assembly Resolution 2758 to prevent Taiwan from participating in international organizations, Zhang rejected the claims as a distortion of facts. She said Resolution 2758 made clear that restoring the lawful rights of the PRC is essential both for the protection of the UN Charter and for the cause that the UN must serve under the Charter. Zhang added that the Taiwan authorities' repeated attempts to distort and attack Resolution 2758 and challenge the authority of the UN and the postwar international order were bound to fail. The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 2758 in 1971 by an overwhelming majority, clarifying that the PRC government is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. This resolution, from the perspective of international law, completely eliminated possibilities of "two Chinas" or "Taiwan independence." Related Stories

item.title: China Coast Guard conducts routine patrols east of Taiwan Island
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
China Coast Guard conducts routine patrols east of Taiwan Island Source: chinadaily.com.cnUpdated: 2026-09-29
The China Coast Guard conducted routine law enforcement patrols in waters east of Taiwan Island on Tuesday, according to the coast guard. Jiang Lue, spokesman for the China Coast Guard, said the CCG task group led by CCGS Zhujiajian carried out the patrols in accordance with the law on Tuesday. Since the beginning of September, the task group has continued to strengthen control over the relevant waters, helping maintain normal navigation and operational order, and safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests, as well as the lives and property, of Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots, Jiang said. The China Coast Guard will continue to strengthen law enforcement patrols in waters under China's jurisdiction and resolutely safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, he added. Related Stories

item.title: Support urged for HK, Macao, Taiwan compatriots, overseas Chinese to contribute to Chinese modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Support urged for HK, Macao, Taiwan compatriots, overseas Chinese to contribute to Chinese modernization Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- A senior Communist Party of China (CPC) official on Monday called on the China Overseas Friendship Association to actively support compatriots from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, as well as overseas Chinese, in contributing to Chinese modernization. Li Ganjie, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the United Front Work Department of the CPC Central Committee, made the remarks at an executive directors' meeting of the association in Beijing. The China Overseas Friendship Association was founded in 1997 to step up contacts between people in the Chinese mainland and those living in Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and abroad. It is a non-profit social organization voluntarily formed by representatives from various sectors and relevant organizations in the mainland, compatriots from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, and prominent figures among overseas Chinese. Li noted progress made by the association over the past year in uniting the Chinese people at home and abroad and promoting exchanges and cooperation with Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan compatriots and overseas Chinese, stressing the need to make winning hearts and rallying strength a priority in its work. Efforts should focus on advancing the successful practice of the "one country, two systems" principle, and playing an active role in driving economic development, fostering social harmony and enhancing effective governance in Hong Kong and Macao, Li said. He also underscored the need to safeguard and promote national reunification, firmly oppose separatist activities by "Taiwan independence" forces, and promote exchanges and cooperation between China and other countries. Related Stories

item.title: Roundup: Chinese mainland welcomes more discussion from Taiwan on reunification
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Roundup: Chinese mainland welcomes more discussion from Taiwan on reunification BEIJING, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese mainland welcomes more discussion in Taiwan on national reunification and is willing to conduct broad and in-depth democratic consultations with people from various sectors on the island on relations across the Taiwan Strait and the future of the Chinese nation, a mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference when commenting on a recent article by a Taiwan scholar suggesting that the mainland should explore ways to end hostility and build mutual trust across the Taiwan Strait before reunification. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China (PRC) was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Zhu said that peaceful reunification and "one country, two systems" remain the basic policy for resolving the Taiwan question and the best way to achieve national reunification. She said the Taiwan plan under a proposed "one country, two systems" framework would fully take into account Taiwan's realities, absorb opinions and suggestions from people on both sides of the Strait, and consider the interests and feelings of Taiwan compatriots. "On the common political basis of adhering to the 1992 Consensus and opposing 'Taiwan independence,' we are willing to carry out broad and in-depth democratic consultations with political parties, groups and people from all sectors in Taiwan on cross-Strait relations and the future of the Chinese nation," Zhu said. She added that the mainland welcomes suggestions from Taiwan compatriots on advancing national reunification, saying that earlier and broader discussions on reunification could create more opportunities for Taiwan's economic and social development and bring more tangible benefits to Taiwan compatriots. Her remarks came as a recent annual survey on cross-Strait relations in Taiwan showed that more than 60 percent of respondents supported continuing cross-Strait exchange platforms, expanding tourist exchanges and increasing exchanges in areas such as film, arts and sports. Zhu said the findings demonstrated that peace, development, exchanges and cooperation remain the mainstream public opinion in Taiwan and a broad consensus among different sectors in Taiwan. She said the mainland will continue to uphold the principle that people on both sides of the Strait are one family, roll out more policies and measures benefiting Taiwan compatriots, strengthen institutional support for cross-Strait integrated development, and promote personnel exchanges and cooperation in various fields. Separately, Zhu said the mainland would continue to promote cross-Strait economic exchanges and cooperation so that people on both sides of the Strait can share the benefits of peaceful and integrated development of cross-Strait relations. She noted that relevant parties on both sides have been working to implement 10 policy measures announced by the mainland in April to promote cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, helping more Taiwan farmers and fishermen expand into the mainland market. According to Zhu, multiple Taiwan packaging plants, orchards and food enterprises have been registered on the mainland, while customs clearance efficiency has improved and logistics have become more convenient. On transportation links, Zhu said direct cross-Strait passenger air services have yet to fully return to normal due to obstruction and interference by the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities. From January to August this year, 4.22 million passenger trips were made on direct cross-Strait flights, up 12.9 percent year on year, reflecting strong market demand and a strong desire for exchanges among people on both sides of the Strait, Zhu said. She called on the Taiwan side to remove unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transportation and allow airlines on both sides to arrange flights based on market demand. Commenting on the annual Shanghai-Taipei City Forum, Zhu described it as an important platform for city-to-city exchanges across the Strait and said both cities had remained in communication over arrangements for this year's event. The forum, which has been held for 16 consecutive years, has developed well-established practices and is expected to proceed as scheduled this year, she said. In response to recent remarks by Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te on increasing Taiwan's "defense spending" to "safeguard peace through strength," Zhu reiterated the mainland's position that there is only one China in the world and Taiwan is part of China. She said the DPP authorities' stubborn pursuit of "Taiwan independence," deliberate escalation of confrontation across the Taiwan Strait, and attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" through military means and external support make them the chief culprit in undermining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. No matter how much is spent on military budgets or weapons purchases, Zhu said, it cannot change the historical trend toward national reunification.

item.title: Taiwan's Kuma Academy criticized for promoting separatism and wartime atmosphere
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Taiwan's Kuma Academy criticized for promoting separatism and wartime atmosphere The Chinese mainland on Wednesday criticized the Kuma Academy in Taiwan for stoking a wartime atmosphere and engaging in separatist activities under the guise of making a profit, calling the organization a "Taiwan independence profiteer". Zhu Fenglian, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said the academy's misconduct was deplorable and warned that separatist activities in pursuit of "Taiwan independence" would be met with punishment. The Kuma Academy recently called on cities and counties across Taiwan to incorporate "wartime disaster preparedness" into local disaster-prevention planning and advocated building a more comprehensive whole-of-society "defense" system on the island. "The remarks are completely misguided and amount to promoting the idea of turning Taiwan into a battlefield, which will inevitably face opposition from the people of Taiwan," Zhu said. She stated that the Kuma Academy had gone to great lengths to stoke a wartime atmosphere and cultivate a "seed of violence" in Taiwan society while openly engaging in separatist activities, making it a de facto base for "Taiwan independence". Zhu added that the organization uses the guise of lectures, training programs, and outdoor exercises to profit from its activities and colludes with external forces to defraud people of their money, making it a "Taiwan independence profiteer".

item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.
